subject.title: Feature: Trigger model fallback on context length exceeded

question: Should unrecoverable context overflow be allowed to cross the active-model boundary, or must OpenClaw keep overflow recovery limited to compaction and a blocked result?
rationale: The present boundary was intentional to prevent a fallback with a smaller effective context window from making recovery worse; changing it requires a durable decision about candidate eligibility, replay safety, and what model change is visible to the user.

options.title: Add guarded larger-window fallback
options.body: After compaction recovery is exhausted, permit only candidates whose effective context budget can accommodate the prepared request, with replay-safe retry and explicit diagnostics.

options.title: Keep compaction-only overflow recovery
options.body: Retain the present boundary and improve the terminal recovery guidance instead of switching models automatically.

options.title: Design candidate eligibility first
options.body: Land the shared context-window-aware candidate-selection contract with the related issue before choosing whether overflow itself may trigger it.

recommendation.title: Add guarded larger-window fallback
recommendation.body: After compaction recovery is exhausted, permit only candidates whose effective context budget can accommodate the prepared request, with replay-safe retry and explicit diagnostics.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent issue review and fallback/embedded-runner history place this policy decision closest to the current recovery-path ownership.
